phase_name: AESIC-001 Idempotency and Restart Repair Independent Verification
summary: Phase 147L.6 was authorized to independently verify AESIC-001 v1.3 (Phase 147L.5's repair) against the two findings finalized by Phase 147L.4: Finding A (Major, the Stage 2 idempotency no-op branch could silently discard a validated stage_1_result, contradicting AESIC-REQ-057's mandatory-when-supplied guarantee) and Finding B (Minor, the restart matrix had no row for a crash between the AER's compound-key commit and the canonical pointer's own write). Both findings were independently reconstructed from primary sources -- the pre-repair v1.2 text, AEMIC-001 section 6's AuthorityEvaluationOutcome shape, and Phase 147L.4's own concrete failure scenario -- before comparing against Phase 147L.5's own repair narrative. Finding A is confirmed closed by AESIC-REQ-129's Stage-1-evidence-equivalence definition, made a precondition of the AESIC-REQ-023(a)/121 no-op classification, verified complete, ordered, deterministic, closed, and implementation-independent against 18 independently constructed adversarial scenarios. Finding B is confirmed closed by AESIC-REQ-130/131 and two new section 11.2 restart-matrix rows, verified against an independently reconstructed nine-step persistence sequence (no structurally possible crash boundary left unspecified) and 16 independently constructed post-AER/pre-pointer adversarial scenarios. This verification's own fresh adversarial pass -- 18 Stage 1 idempotency scenarios, 7 concurrency scenarios, 9 replay/restart scenarios, 16 post-AER/pre-pointer scenarios, a full falsification attempt against all 14 named architectural invariants, and 14 independent threat categories -- found no new Blocking, Major, or Minor finding. Two Informational observations are reported: return-value semantics under a lost concurrent-pointer race are not explicitly stated in the contract text, though unambiguously derivable from existing text and consistent with the already-accepted IWPC-REQ-144/147 last-write-wins precedent; and a pre-existing, out-of-scope AEMIC-001 field-count/table discrepancy (AEMIC-REQ-021's header says eight fields, its own table lists nine) was surfaced by this phase's independent-re-derivation method but is orthogonal to AESIC-001's own correctness and out of this phase's No-Go Boundary to repair. No predecessor-contract amendment is required (AEM-001, AEMIC-001, IWC-001, IWPC-001, PEC-001, CHGR-001 independently re-confirmed unaffected). fast_green 4391/4391 and the 183 authority-evaluation tests both passed unchanged; no production, schema, test, or contract file was touched. Overall Verdict: AESIC-001 v1.3 INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED. Recommends 147M (Authority Evaluation Integration Implementation), not itself an authorization.
tests_added_or_updated: No test file was added or modified by this phase. The existing tests/test_phase_147g_authority_evaluation.py and tests/test_phase_147h_authority_evaluation_independent_verification.py suites, and the fast_green marker suite, were run unchanged to confirm no regression, since this phase performed verification-only analysis.

validation_results.name: phase_147l6_finding_a_reconstruction
validation_results.result: Independently reconstructed Finding A's exact concrete failure scenario from Phase 147L.4's own section 17: a canonical AER with no stage_1_outcome_ref exists; a later attempt supplies genuinely valid Stage 1 evidence; citation/outcome fields are otherwise unchanged; pre-repair AESIC-REQ-121 classifies this unchanged and AESIC-REQ-023(a) returns the existing AER, discarding the newly supplied evidence. Confirmed AESIC-REQ-129's one-absent-one-present rule is the minimal, sufficient repair.

validation_results.name: phase_147l6_finding_b_reconstruction
validation_results.result: Independently reconstructed Finding B from Phase 147L.4's own section 17: AER persistence is structurally two sequential writes (compound-key commit, then pointer write); a crash between them was previously undescribed by section 11.2's table, violating AESIC-REQ-103's completeness guarantee. Confirmed AESIC-REQ-130's uncommitted-candidate, recovery-is-retry rule is sufficient: durable state named precisely, classified without ambiguity, discovered through the existing AESIC-REQ-023 comparison, and forecloses inferring canonicity from recency.

validation_results.name: phase_147l6_stage1_idempotency_equivalence_verification
validation_results.result: AESIC-REQ-129 independently confirmed complete, ordered, deterministic, closed, implementation-independent, and resistant to ambiguous comparison: every reachable Stage 1 evidence state pair falls into exactly one of three mutually exclusive branches; evaluation_id's exclusion independently confirmed necessary (its per-invocation uniqueness would otherwise make every Stage 1 invocation permanently not-equivalent to any other, defeating idempotency).

validation_results.name: phase_147l6_stage1_adversarial_analysis
validation_results.result: Constructed and traced all 18 Stage 1 idempotency scenarios named in the authorizing prompt's section 5: every scenario resolves to exactly one deterministic outcome (no-op reuse, supersession, or refusal); scenarios differing only in session/identity/template are correctly intercepted one layer earlier by AESIC-REQ-123 before AESIC-REQ-129 is ever reached.

validation_results.name: phase_147l6_concurrency_verification
validation_results.result: Constructed and traced all 7 concurrency scenarios named in the authorizing prompt's section 7: deterministic winner selection (atomic-replace guarantees a total order), no silent loss of valid Stage 1 evidence (every primary-store write is independent of the pointer race and none is ever deleted), no mutable AER history, no multiple current-effective pointers, no compound-key corruption, and observational equivalence after retry, all independently confirmed without assuming any specific filesystem, database, lock, or transaction implementation.

validation_results.name: phase_147l6_replay_restart_verification
validation_results.result: Constructed and traced all 9 replay/restart scenarios named in the authorizing prompt's section 8: Stage 1 evidence encoded in the AER remains retrievable, no transient Stage-1-only storage is required, the idempotency comparison is deterministically repeatable, and replay cannot silently substitute one Stage 1 history for another without supersession.

validation_results.name: phase_147l6_post_aer_pre_pointer_recovery_verification
validation_results.result: Independently re-derived the persistence sequence from AESIC-REQ-119 (two durable writes: compound-key commit, then pointer write, both atomic) and confirmed AESIC-REQ-130/131 fully close Finding B: durable post-crash state named and shown never mistaken for corrupt, canonical, or lost; recovery-is-retry uses no new mechanism beyond the existing AESIC-REQ-023 comparison; a retry can never overwrite a legitimately newer canonical pointer because it always reads the current pointer fresh.

validation_results.name: phase_147l6_restart_matrix_completeness_verification
validation_results.result: Mapped the authorizing prompt's nine-step persistence sequence against every possible crash boundary independently: both atomic-write boundaries (AER commit, pointer write) collapse their during-state into before/after by construction, leaving exactly the one new crash window AESIC-REQ-130 names plus the disjoint AESIC-REQ-131 synchronous-failure case. No structurally possible restart point remains unspecified, matching Phase 147L.5's own section 33.2 disposition, independently re-derived rather than assumed.

validation_results.name: phase_147l6_post_aer_pre_pointer_adversarial_analysis
validation_results.result: Constructed and traced all 16 post-AER/pre-pointer adversarial scenarios named in the authorizing prompt's section 11: no scenario produces an undefined, ambiguous, or contradictory outcome; CanonicalPointerUpdateFailedError and CanonicalPointerCorruptError independently confirmed structurally disjoint and non-overlapping.

validation_results.name: phase_147l6_error_taxonomy_verification
validation_results.result: Independently confirmed CanonicalPointerUpdateFailedError and CanonicalPointerCorruptError are distinct, exhaustive for their intended cases, and carry no ownership gap or dual authority across origin, detection, recovery, retry, logging, and user-visible dimensions. Partial success (AER durable, pointer unavailable) is confirmed represented via a raised exception, never a false success return.
